title: Three-Tier Gate Matrix & Release-Notes Orchestration for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Define a three-tier release gate matrix (Traffic-Light: Green/Amber/Red) and an integrated release-notes orchestration process that aligns API, Console, and Runtime teams. Deliverables: 1) gate matrix with measurable signals and owners, 2) canonical release-notes template and staging workflow, 3) a synchronous launch runway checklist tying milestones to marketing/partner comms. Rationale: Prior launches exposed gaps in cross-team signal definition (what counts as a 'release-readiness' regression), and inconsistent release note formats slowed comms. This ticket unblocks coordinated launches and reduces last-minute scope debates by codifying cut criteria per tier and providing a single source of truth for release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Gate matrix (Green/Amber/Red) published with signal thresholds, owners, and escalation paths documented in Confluence
Release-notes canonical template created and approved by PM, ENG, and Design
A staged release-notes workflow established (Draft -> Legal/Compliance review -> Engineering sign-off -> Marketing-ready) with assigned owners
Cut criteria defined per milestone and enforced via pre-flight checklist; triage playbook for Amber/Red states created
Cross-team kickoffs scheduled and templates shared; at least two stakeholders have run a dry-run on the checklist
tasks: Draft gate matrix and scorecard (PM owner)
Gather signal inputs: latency P50/P95, error budget burn, e2e smoke test pass rate, console UX regressions, migration blockers
Design release-notes template and examples for API/Console/Runtime
Define review workflow and SLAs for each review step (legal, security, docs, marketing)
Integrate release-notes draft into release train calendar and create calendar reminders
Coordinate a cross-team dry-run for milestone M1 with simulated Amber condition
Publish final docs and link to ship checklist and rollout runbook
rollout_plan: Tier 1 (Green): All signals nominal; automatic proceed with standard release notes. Owner: PM
Tier 2 (Amber): One or more non-critical signals degraded (e.g., P95 latency spike <30% over baseline); require canary extension and decision call. Owner: ENG lead + PM
Tier 3 (Red): Critical signal tripped (error budget >70% consumed, critical regressions in runtime kernel); block release until rollback or mitigation validated. Owner: ENG director + PM + Security
Escalation path: On Amber or Red, page on-call, schedule 30-minute Triage, and open a short-lived incident channel; log decision and follow up actions in the release ticket
Rollout slices: API endpoints first (limited customer orgs), Console update second (internal beta), Runtime hotfix last (if needed) to allow safe rollback

notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-03-15: Use three-tier traffic-light model instead of binary go/no-go to provide graded responses and reduce launch churn.
Decision 2025-03-17: Release-notes will include a machine-readable changelog section (Y/N fields) to support automated downstream publishing to docs and partner portals.
Trade-off: Stricter Green thresholds reduce risk but increase number of Amber triages. We agreed to conservative Green for runtime signals and more permissive Green for non-critical console metrics.
